parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آن بآن, from Persian [Term?], from Arabic آن (ʔān).

parole.significato: some; an unspecified quantity or number of.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish بعضی (ba'zı), from Persian بعضی (ba'zi), from Arabic بَعْض (baʕḍ).
From Ottoman Turkish بر طرف (ber taraf), from Persian بر (bar) and Arabic طَرَف (ṭaraf).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خامور (hamur), from Persian خمیر (xamir), from Arabic خَمِير (ḵamīr).

From Ottoman Turkish خارق العاده, from Persian خارقالعاده (xâreqo-l-'âde), from Arabic خَارِقُ العَادَة (ḵāriqu al-ʕāda), equivalent to harika + adet. Compare Azerbaijani xariqüladə, Crimean Tatar harikulade and Uzbek xoriqulodda.
From Ottoman Turkish خصمانه (hasmane), from Persian خصمانه (xasmâne), from Arabic خَصْم (ḵaṣm).

From Ottoman Turkish هر شی, from now dated Persian هر شیء (har šey', “everything”, literally “each thing”), from هر (har, “each, every”) + شیء (“thing, object”), the latter being a borrowing from Arabic شَيْء (šayʔ, “thing”).

parole.significato: Honorific title given to the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
parole.testo: From Persian انسان کامل (ensân-e kâmel), from Arabic الْإِنْسَان الْكَامِل (al-ʔinsān al-kāmil, literally “the person who has reached perfection”).
From Ottoman Turkish قلاش (kallâš), from Persian قلاش (qallâš), from Arabic قَلَّاش (qallāš), from Persian کلاش (kallâš).

parole.significato: (of an animal or a plant) Having been bred from two different species; hybrid, half-bred.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملز (melez, “mixed, half-bred, mongrel”), from Persian ملس (“sweet and sour, twilight, cotton-silk mix fabric, bastard”), from Arabic مَلَس (malas, “twilight”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مؤذن (müezzin), derived from Persian مؤذن (mo'azzen), derived from Arabic مُؤَذِّن (muʔaḏḏin, “muezzin”).
From Ottoman Turkish صمیمی (samimi), from Persian صمیمی (samimi), or formed like it in Ottoman Turkish from Arabic صَمِيم (ṣamīm, “marrow, core”).

parole.significato: A bagel or ring doughnut shaped bread roll covered with sesame seeds.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سمید (simit), from Persian سمید (semid, “semolina”), from Arabic سَمِيد (samīd, “semolina”), from Aramaic סְמִידָא / ܣܡܻܝܕܳܐ (səmīḏā), from Akkadian 𒆠𒅔𒆠𒅔𒄯𒄯 (/⁠samīdu⁠/, “a type of fine groats, coarse flour, semolina”), related to Akkadian 𒀀𒊏𒄯𒄯 (/⁠samādu⁠/, “to grind fine”).
From Ottoman Turkish سفره, صوفره (sofra), from Persian سفره (sofre) from Arabic سُفْرَة (sufra).
From Ottoman Turkish سوقاق, from Persian زقاق, from Arabic زُقَاق (zuqāq).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طاقت (takat), from Persian طاقت (tâqat), from Arabic طَاقَة (ṭāqa).
From Persian تهدید (tahdid), from Arabic تَهْدِيد (tahdīd).

parole.significato: A dish made by adding fried or stale bread into gravy.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تریت (terit, tirit, “a sop of bread, moistened with gravy and stewed”), shares common origin with Persian ترید (tarid, “bread moistened with milk or water”), from Arabic ثَرِيد (ṯarīd, “dish of bread in broth”).

parole.significato: ginger, any flowering plant of the species Zingiber officinale
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنجفیل (zencefil), from Classical Persian زنجفیل (zanjafīl), from Arabic زَنْجَبِيل (zanjabīl), from Classical Syriac ܙܢܓܒܝܠ (zangabīl), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀺𑀁𑀕𑀺𑀯𑁂𑀭 (siṃgivera), ultimately from Old Tamil 𑀇𑀜𑁆𑀘𑀺𑀯𑁂𑀭𑁆 (iñcivēr).
From Ottoman Turkish شمعدان (şemʼdan), from Persian شمعدان (šam'dân), compound of the Arabic شَمْع (šamʕ) + Persian ـدان (-dân).
